dct_description_sm: The main objective of this multiyear project was to develop a climate change adaptation plan that lists the vulnerabilities, opportunities, and strategies to respond to climate change in the selected region. The project also aimed to create a useful and practical planning document and to complete an adaptation plan that achieved the following: - built on traditional Gwichin knowledge; - complemented existing planning processes; - responded to community priorities; - built community adaptive capacity; and - started implementation as soon was possible The project also held a regional permafrost degradation workshop in Inuvik in January 2010, as one of its objectives.   In the second year, work continued with implementing the Tsiigehtchic adaptation plan. The focus of the plan was to adapt to mudslides and erosion on Church Hill. In addition, the project initiated the adaptation planning process within the community of Fort McPherson, focussing on the vulnerability of the land, economy, people, and infrastructure to climate change, with a special emphasis on infrastructure foundations and their vulnerability to permafrost degradation.
